subject: music
topicDisplay: Area Of Study 1 My Music Performance
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is 'syncopation'?
options: Placing accents on weak or off beats
questions.explain: Syncopation stresses normally weak beats or off-beats, disrupting the regular pulse.

questions.q: Two quavers together are worth the same as one:
questions.explain: Two quavers equal one crotchet beat.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the operas 'The Marriage of Figaro' and 'The Magic Flute' during the Classical period?
questions.explain: Mozart, a leading Classical-period composer, wrote both 'The Marriage of Figaro' and 'The Magic Flute'.

questions.q: A minor triad is built from which intervals above the root?
questions.explain: A minor triad stacks a minor 3rd then a major 3rd, giving its darker sound.

questions.q: A 'fusion' genre is one that:
options: Blends elements of two or more musical styles
questions.explain: Fusion combines features of two or more different musical styles or traditions.

questions.q: 'Quantising' in a DAW is used to:
options: Correct the timing of notes onto the beat
questions.explain: Quantising snaps recorded notes to the nearest beat to tidy up their timing.

questions.q: The Baroque composer who wrote 'The Four Seasons', a set of concertos, was:
questions.explain: Antonio Vivaldi composed 'The Four Seasons', a famous set of Baroque violin concertos.

questions.q: 'Polyphonic' (or contrapuntal) texture means:
options: Two or more independent melodic lines sounding together
questions.explain: Polyphonic texture combines two or more independent melodic lines.

questions.q: In the mnemonic 'MAD T-SHIRT' for the elements of music, what does the 'I' stand for?
questions.explain: In 'MAD T-SHIRT' the I stands for instrumentation, meaning the choice of instruments and voices used.

questions.q: What does the dynamic marking 'mezzo-forte' (mf) mean?
questions.explain: Mezzo-forte means moderately loud, sitting between piano and forte.

questions.q: Which composer is most associated with the Baroque period?
questions.explain: J.S. Bach is a leading Baroque composer; Beethoven bridged Classical and Romantic.

questions.q: In a DAW, 'automation' is most commonly used to:
options: Make settings like volume or panning change automatically over time
questions.explain: Automation lets parameters such as volume or panning change automatically across a track over time.

questions.q: Why is tuning important before an ensemble performs?
options: So all players sound in pitch with each other
questions.explain: Tuning ensures all players' pitches match so the ensemble sounds in tune together.

questions.q: 'Scat singing' in jazz is:
questions.explain: Scat singing uses improvised, wordless nonsense syllables as a vocal solo.

questions.q: Reggae music, with its characteristic offbeat 'skank' chords, originated in:
questions.explain: Reggae developed in Jamaica and features offbeat chord chops known as the skank.

questions.q: A 'reprise' in a musical or song means:
options: A repeat or return of an earlier song or theme
questions.explain: A reprise is the return or repeat of music heard earlier in the work.

questions.q: Romantic music (c1810-1910) is generally noted for:
options: Strong emotional expression and large orchestras
questions.explain: Romantic music emphasises emotion, expression and often larger orchestras.

questions.q: A repeated rhythmic or melodic pattern, common in world and minimalist music, is an:
questions.explain: An ostinato is a persistently repeated musical pattern.

questions.q: A chromatic scale moves entirely in:
questions.explain: A chromatic scale ascends or descends entirely in semitones, using all twelve pitches.

questions.q: Which cadence ends on chord V, sounding unfinished?
questions.explain: An imperfect cadence ends on chord V and sounds incomplete.

questions.q: Which group of instruments typically forms the 'rhythm section' of a band?
questions.explain: The rhythm section usually consists of drums, bass and a chordal instrument like guitar or keyboard.

questions.q: 'Walking bass' is a feature most associated with which style?
questions.explain: A walking bass line moving steadily in crotchets is a characteristic jazz feature.
